Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud's results for the Q3 2024. With me on the call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; Maya Singh, Chief Technology Officer; Liam Patel, Chief Product Officer; and Sophia Reyes, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud delivered another strong Q3, marked by significant growth in our core cloud business and increasing adoption of our innovative AI solutions.

During the quarter, our priorities were focused on six key areas:
1. Expanding our global cloud infrastructure footprint.
2. Driving innovation in serverless computing.
3. Enhancing our cybersecurity offerings.
4. Strengthening our partnerships with leading ISVs.
5. Improving customer satisfaction and retention.
6. Investing in our talent pool and fostering a culture of innovation.

One of our standout strategic pillars this quarter has been our push on energy efficiency and sustainability initiatives, which are integral to our hyperscale operations and long-term competitive edge. In cloud computing, data centers consume about 2-3% of global electricity today, with projections hitting 8% by 2030 per the IEA, so these efforts drive efficiency, compliance, retention, and margins. At Nexara Cloud, we've made them core to our infrastructure strategy, outperforming peers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud in the ESG arena.

Key wins include a fleet-wide Power Usage Effectiveness of 1.12 across our 28 global data centers, improved from 1.18 last year and beating the 1.50 industry average from Uptime Institute—this cut energy OpEx by 15%, or $145 million annualized. Water Usage Effectiveness is at 0.18 liters per kWh, down 22% YoY via closed-loop cooling in Arizona and Virginia. Emissions-wise, we're at 95% renewable matching, up from 82%, through 2.5 GW in PPAs with partners like Ørsted and NextEra, dropping Scope 1 and 2 GHG by 28% to 1.2 million metric tons CO2e despite 42% compute growth supporting 35% revenue rise.

This stems from a comprehensive roadmap: hardware shifts with 65% of instances on our Nexara Graviton ARM processors, offering 40% better efficiency per core than x86, and 2.8x performance per watt in AI/ML—aiming for 80% ARM by 2025 for $200 million more savings. Cooling advances include direct-to-chip liquid systems in 12 sites, cutting energy 45%, like our 1.08 PUE Singapore hub with Vertiv, and immersion pilots in Oregon for GPU clusters. Software like Nexara Optimizer uses reinforcement learning to right-size workloads, slashing idle waste 32% to 12 gCO2e/kWh carbon intensity, half the grid average, boosting customer TCO 25-30% and Green Cloud tier to 28% of bookings.

Regionally tailored: North America's IAD and PDX are 100% renewable with solar-storage and hydro, dodging Texas volatility for 99.999% uptime. EMEA's Frankfurt and Paris hit 98% renewables from Nordic wind, with hour-on-hour carbon-free pilots securing DAX 40 deals at 40% lower Scope 3 than AWS. APAC's modular edge sites in Mumbai, Jakarta, Sydney integrate solar, achieving 150 gCO2e/kWh vs. regional 450, fueling 55% growth.

These margin-boosting moats—78% gross margins now—include ESG contracts with 72% of Fortune 500 at 5-10% premiums ($320 million Q3 ARR), ahead on SEC and ISSB rules. Our 2030 net-zero plan: carbon-free by 2026, 50% emissions cut amid 3x capacity, $500 million R&D in quantum-efficient tech, 5 GW more PPAs, Schneider partnerships. With $2.5 billion reserve against chip constraints and REC volatility, we're greening the cloud profitably in a $1.5 trillion market by 2030.

Now I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez to provide a detailed review of our financial performance.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q3 2024. Revenue increased by 22% year-over-year to $29.2 billion, driven by strong demand for our cloud services. Our gross margin was 78%, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency. Our operating margin was 36%.

Good afternoon, everyone. Let's dive into our Q3 total revenue performance, which came in at $29.2 billion, representing a strong beat against our guidance range of $28.5 billion to $28.8 billion issued last quarter. This $400 million exceedance on the high end underscores the accelerating demand tailwinds in our core cloud workloads, particularly around generative AI and high-performance computing. Year-over-year, total revenue grew 22%, up from $23.9 billion in Q3 FY2023, outpacing our initial expectations of 18% to 20% growth and marking our 11th straight quarter of at least 20% YoY expansion.

To give you the full picture, let me break this down by segment and drivers. Infrastructure and Platform revenue—our IaaS and PaaS offerings, including NexCompute virtual machines, NexStorage block/object storage, and NexPlatform for Kubernetes-orchestrated containers—accounted for 72% of total revenue at $21.0 billion, up 25% YoY. This was fueled by a 35% surge in GPU-accelerated instances, where we've seen hyperscale customers like a leading social media platform ramping deployments of our NexAI Clusters integrated with NVIDIA H100s and now early previews of Blackwell GPUs. Storage revenue specifically grew 28% YoY to $6.8 billion, driven by exabyte-scale data lakes for analytics workloads, as enterprises migrate from on-premises Hadoop clusters to our fully managed Apache Iceberg-compatible services.

Our higher-margin SaaS and data services, including NexAnalytics for real-time BI and NexML for AutoML pipelines, delivered $8.2 billion, or 28% of total revenue, growing 18% YoY. Here, we saw particular strength in usage-based pricing models, with average revenue per enterprise customer up 12% sequentially due to expanded seat licenses and API call volumes from fine-tuning large language models.

Regionally, the Americas remained our growth engine at $16.8 billion, or 58% of total, with 24% YoY growth, propelled by major net new wins in financial services—think wins against legacy Oracle and SAP deployments—and public sector deals under our FedRAMP High authorized sovereign cloud. EMEA contributed $7.1 billion, up 21% YoY, though slightly tempered by FX headwinds from a stronger USD; excluding FX, it was 24% growth, boosted by GDPR-compliant data residency zones in Frankfurt and Paris, where we've captured share from smaller regional providers. APAC was the standout at $5.3 billion, surging 19% YoY—or 23% CC—thanks to our Tokyo and Singapore multi-region latency optimizations, which have helped us land hyperscaler expansions from e-commerce giants akin to Alibaba and JD.com, plus early sovereign cloud pilots in India ahead of data localization mandates.

A few key trends and initiatives worth highlighting: First, AI inference workloads now represent 22% of our overall compute utilization, up from 14% a year ago, as customers shift from training to production-scale serving with tools like our NexServe inference engine, which delivers 40% better TCO than comparable AWS SageMaker endpoints. We've also seen a 15% YoY increase in remaining performance obligations (RPO) to $142 billion, signaling multi-year commitments in hybrid cloud scenarios. Strategically, our NexEdge portfolio for 5G telco edge computing added $450 million in new bookings, partnering with Ericsson and Nokia to deploy low-latency VNFs, while sustainability efforts—like our 100% renewable-matched energy in US West regions—have differentiated us in ESG-focused RFPs, closing deals 20% faster.

Looking back, we guided conservatively to account for potential enterprise budget scrutiny amid high interest rates, but customer acceleration in AI capex—echoing what we've seen across peers like AWS's 19% growth and Azure's run rate—proved those concerns overstated. This beat positions us well for Q4, where we're guiding total revenue to $30.1 billion to $30.4 billion, implying 21% to 23% YoY growth, with continued margin expansion from operating leverage in our data centers.

Next, I'd like to introduce Maya Singh, who will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Maya Singh:
Thank you, Elena. On the technology front, we made significant progress in several areas. We successfully launched our next-generation NexCompute platform, which offers enhanced performance and scalability.

Thank you, Jordan, and good afternoon, everyone. As we highlight our operational excellence, I want to focus on our data breach prevention and incident response measures—one of our foundational strengths in securing multi-trillion-dollar workloads against rivals like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. We've invested $750 million in security R&D over three years, 12% of OpEx up from 8% in 2021, yielding zero material breaches in 24 months, 45% fewer high-severity incidents QoQ, and MTTD down to 4.2 minutes from 12.

Our zero-trust architecture per NIST 800-207 micro-segments everything, powered by Nexara Shield AI/ML on 15 petabytes of telemetry from 2.5 million instances—blocking 2.8 billion attacks in Q3, up 32% YoY amid ransomware surges per CrowdStrike.

Prevention layers: Endpoint/network with CrowdStrike Falcon, Prisma Cloud at 99.99% efficacy, 98.7% zero-days blocked. Data security via quantum-resistant Kyber/Dilithium on 85% storage, AES-256-GCM, enforced client-side for regulated data. Identity with passwordless FIDO2, SPIFFE/SPIRE cutting lateral risks 60%. Compliance automated 92% for SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP via Drata, saving 35% on audits.

Ahead on AI threats—Gartner says 75% enterprises hit by 2025—our GenAI sandbox isolates LLMs, thwarting prompt injections in 1.4 million sessions. Regionally: Americas HIPAA/PCI with SBOM scanning; EMEA GDPR at 99.5% residency for Deutsche Bank wins; APAC PDPA/PIPL with air-gapped backups stopping 1,200 incidents. This lifts NPS to 78, 10 above AWS, adding $180 million security upsell ARR.

Response via NIST 800-61r2 SOAR with Splunk Phantom: MTTR 18 minutes for P1, containment <2 hours 96%. Global SOCs in Ashburn, Singapore, Frankfurt with 450 analysts, Chaos drills at 95%. Immutable snapshots for 5-min RPO/15-min RTO, restoring 10PB in 47 minutes simulated. Mandiant MDR, CISA feeds, $4.2 million HackerOne bounties.

This moat captures $125 billion security spend by 2027 with 65% margin bundles at $0.02/GB/month, 98.7% retention. Q4 CapEx $120 million for enclaves, homomorphic pilots amid DORA/SEC rules—safeguarding 40 zettabytes for 15-20% CAGR.

Now, I'll pass it over to Liam Patel for a product roadmap update.

Liam Patel:
Thank you, Maya. We are excited about the market reception to our new NexAI offering. This product is designed to address the evolving needs of our customers in the AI/ML sector.

Thank you, Operator, and good afternoon, everyone. This is Liam Patel here, but before opening for Q&A, let me outline the key assumptions underpinning our FY25 revenue and profitability forecasts—the bedrock of our guidance: $145-150 billion revenue, 22-26% YoY growth midpoint, adjusted operating income $52-56 billion, non-GAAP EPS $8.45-8.75.

Stress-tested against macro headwinds like rates and geopolitics, plus AI tailwinds, revenue drivers include: Core IaaS/PaaS (75%) at 25-28% growth, ARR $85 billion +31% YoY, RPO $220 billion +42% at 92% conversion. GPU util 85-90% via Nexara Trainium3 (4x inference, 60% cheaper H100s), 40% AI growth, $15 billion hyperscaler sovereign commitments, no delays in 20 data centers.

SaaS/analytics (15%) 18-22%, Nexara Analytics with Snowflake/Databricks, 15% attach, ARPU $2.5K-$3.2K, 5-7% pricing uplift, 70% consumption-reserved. Emerging (10%) $12-14 billion: Nexara Outposts in 5,000+ 5G sites +50% YoY, quantum-safe NIST PQC, 30% multi-cloud growth, $3 billion GenAI Marketplace at 2 million devs, 25% monetization with Anthropic/Cohere.

Regions: NA 55% 24%, EMEA 25% 28% with 15 sovereigns, APAC 15% 32%, RoW 5% 20%. 18% customer growth to 2.2 million, enterprise 65% at 28%, FX +1%, no big deflation.

Profitability: Gross 38-39% +150 bps from silicon TCO 40% down (75% Trainium/Inferentia), PUE 1.15, 60% carbon-free. OpEx: R&D 12% $17-18B flat %, 25K engineers; S&M 11% $16B leverage 2.8x; total 19% growth to $42-44B, margins 36-37%. FCF $45-50B (32%), CapEx $55-60B (38%) 70/30 build/refresh, 35 regions, 500MW GPUs. $20B buybacks, small M&A like $1.2B Habana.

Risks: +3 pts rev if AI accelerates, -2 if recession; margins ±100 bps CapEx/energy. 10-15% conservatism.

These fuel 1.5x market growth in $1.2T TAM.

I'll now hand it over to Sophia Reyes to discuss our marketing initiatives.

Sophia Reyes:
Thank you, Liam. We have been focused on driving brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly effective in reaching our target audience.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining Nexara Cloud's Q3 2024 earnings call. Today I'll dive deep into our new customer acquisition cost, or CAC, performance—a critical metric tying to scalable growth and profitability. CAC is fully loaded sales/marketing spend per new customer, cohort-based including headcount, commissions, ABM, partners, trials. Dollar-based recovery time was 14 months in Q3, under our 18-month target.

Headline: Blended CAC $218,000 per new customer, 12% YoY decline from $248,000, 5% sequential from Q2's $229,000—sixth straight compression via PLG and sales gains. By tier: Enterprise >$1M ARR $425,000; Mid-Market $100K-$1M $95,000; SMB <$100K $12,500 via freemium.

Breakdown: S&M 28% of bookings vs. 34% YoY. Marketing 42% ($91,000) +18% YoY from 3x ROI AI lead scoring with NexaraAI/Salesforce. Sales 55% ($120,000), cycles 112 days -22% YoY on ABM VMware migrations. Partners 3% +45% YoY via AWS Marketplace StratoEdge, Azure Arc.

Regions: NA 58% logos $192,000 lowest ever -16% YoY, 28% free tier conversions. EMEA $245,000 +4% seq on GDPR but 2.1x LTV telcos. APAC $185,000 -25% YoY, 140 new incl. Reliance Jio sovereign. LatAm nascent $210,000 trending down.

Drivers: PLG 41% new ARR +12 pts, 32% conversions compressing SMB 35%. AI copilots -40% ramp, +15% win rates vs. Vertex. Partners 4.2x payback with Databricks. Composable infra shortens PoCs 60-35 days.

Benchmarks: 4.8x LTV/CAC ($1.05M LTV, 125% NRR) beats AWS 16-20 months, Snowflake 5.2x. AI $200B spend, 62% deals triggered. FY24 CAC $215-220K, 10-15% compress FY25 to 50% PLG, $500M partners. Sub-15 mo payback for $4.2B rev, 32% margins.

This flywheel powers 22% CAGR to $1T by 2028.

Back to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Sophia. We are confident that our strong financial performance, innovative technology, and talented team will enable us to continue to deliver exceptional value to our customers and shareholders.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before we open the line for Q&A, I'd like to address the impact of currency fluctuations on our reported revenue. With over 65% of our $29.2 billion Q3 revenue from outside the U.S.—across IaaS, PaaS, SaaS like NexCore and Nebula AI—we face FX volatility. Adverse moves created a $285 million headwind, 3.8% drag on growth, vs. $210 million 2.9% in Q2, from strong USD and Fed rates.

Regionally: EMEA 28% $5.1B CC hit hardest—EUR -7.2% QoQ $140M loss on German/French sovereign VMware to NexCore; GBP -4.8% on UK NHS £450M lake. APAC 26% $4.8B 42% CC growth mixed: JPY -9.1% $85M on Nebula GPUs, AUD steady +$12M Sydney edge, INR stable for Mumbai fintech 55% ramp. LATAM 12% $2.2B BRL -5.4% $45M despite 38% São Paulo e-com growth.

Ex-FX, international +31% YoY vs. NA 24%, backed by $142B RPO 72% subscriptions. Mitigation: 75-85% hedges gained $62M offsetting 22%; dynamic local pricing to 80% EMEA/APAC cuts 15-20% exposure. Diversifying: EMEA 35% new ARR Nordics; APAC JPY 3-yr locks, $1.2B India/Indonesia. FY25 2-4% headwind at USD 105-110, CC $78-82B 28% growth to $100B ARR FY26.

124% NRR shows resilience; better than AWS 3%, Azure 4.2%.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Thompson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you elaborate more on the contribution from AI workloads to your growth and how that's scaling into inference?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, AI has been a massive tailwind, with inference now at 22% of compute utilization, up from 14% YoY, as customers move to production with NexServe delivering 40% better TCO than SageMaker. Our GPU surge of 35% includes hyperscalers ramping NexAI Clusters with H100s and Blackwell previews, and we've baked 40% of IaaS growth from AI/ML into FY25 assumptions, supported by $15 billion commitments. Scaling remains strong with 85-90% GPU util via Trainium3.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. On margins and CAC, how do you see compression continuing, and any updates to FY25 outlook?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Lisa. CAC at $218K blended, down 12% YoY, with 14-month payback and 4.8x LTV/CAC outperforming peers, driven by 41% PLG, AI sales tools, and partners—we expect $215-220K FY24, 10-15% more compress FY25 targeting 50% PLG. Margins expand to 38-39% gross on efficiencies like 1.15 PUE and silicon shifts, operating to 36-37%, with FCF 32%. FY25 revenue $145-150B firm.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are committed to transparency and open communication with our investors.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
